{
  "subtype": "causal_attribution",
  "outcome_variable": "low_review_score (is_low_score)",
  "per_column": [
    {"name": "is_low_score", "causal_role": "outcome", "named_in_query": true, "rationale": "Binary encoding of the focus variable; the outcome itself, restated from the query."},
    {"name": "helpfulness_ratio", "causal_role": "collider", "named_in_query": false, "rationale": "Helpfulness votes are plausibly caused by review content/score reception rather than causing the score; adjusting for it risks collider bias, not a common cause of the review-writing behavior and the score."},
    {"name": "review_length", "causal_role": "other", "named_in_query": false, "rationale": "A generic text-length feature. It is a property of the review text, correlated with score but not a plausible upstream common cause; closer to a descriptor/proxy than a confounder."},
    {"name": "word_count", "causal_role": "other", "named_in_query": false, "rationale": "Mechanical token count; generic, does not represent a common cause of a treatment and the outcome."},
    {"name": "has_exclamation", "causal_role": "other", "named_in_query": false, "rationale": "Stylistic text feature; a downstream expression of the reviewer's sentiment rather than a common cause; not a confounder."},
    {"name": "has_question", "causal_role": "other", "named_in_query": false, "rationale": "Stylistic text feature, generic; not a common cause of a treatment and the outcome."},
    {"name": "negative_word_count", "causal_role": "mediator", "named_in_query": false, "rationale": "Negative language expresses the reviewer's (dis)satisfaction; it lies on the path between an experience and the assigned score rather than being an upstream common cause. Treating it as a confounder would be an error."},
    {"name": "positive_word_count", "causal_role": "mediator", "named_in_query": false, "rationale": "Same as negative_word_count: sentiment expressed in text is on the causal path to the score, a mediator/proxy of the outcome, not a confounder."},
    {"name": "sentiment_ratio", "causal_role": "mediator", "named_in_query": false, "rationale": "Derived sentiment measure that essentially encodes the same satisfaction that drives the score; mediator/near-outcome, not a common cause."},
    {"name": "summary_length", "causal_role": "other", "named_in_query": false, "rationale": "Generic length feature of the summary text; not a plausible common cause of treatment and outcome."},
    {"name": "caps_ratio", "causal_role": "other", "named_in_query": false, "rationale": "Stylistic emphasis feature; downstream expression of reviewer emotion, not an upstream common cause."},
    {"name": "product_avg_score", "causal_role": "confounder", "named_in_query": false, "rationale": "Underlying product quality plausibly causes both how a given reviewer tends to rate (treatment behavior) and the individual low score outcome; a genuine common cause surfaced from data."},
    {"name": "user_avg_score", "causal_role": "confounder", "named_in_query": false, "rationale": "Reviewer's baseline harshness/leniency causes both their propensity to be a harsh reviewer (treatment) and the low score outcome; a genuine common cause surfaced from data."},
    {"name": "score_vs_product_avg", "causal_role": "collider", "named_in_query": false, "rationale": "Computed as a function of the score itself relative to product average; it is derived from the outcome and thus a collider/near-outcome, not a valid confounder."},
    {"name": "reviewer_is_harsh", "causal_role": "treatment", "named_in_query": false, "rationale": "A binary indicator of reviewer harshness serves as the candidate cause (treatment) whose effect on the low score is being attributed."}
  ],
  "treatment_present": true,
  "treatment_columns": ["reviewer_is_harsh"],
  "confounders": [
    {"name": "product_avg_score", "named_in_query": false, "plausibility": 0.7},
    {"name": "user_avg_score", "named_in_query": false, "plausibility": 0.5}
  ],
  "confounder_quality": 0.4,
  "rationale": "A plausible treatment (reviewer_is_harsh) is present, and the query names no confounders, so any valid common cause counts toward the capability. product_avg_score is a genuine common cause (product quality drives both rating tendency and the low score) surfaced from data. user_avg_score partly overlaps with the harshness treatment (near-definitional to reviewer_is_harsh, which is derived from user_avg_score), weakening it as an independent confounder. The bulk of added columns are generic text/style features, sentiment mediators expressing the same satisfaction that produces the score, or outcome-derived colliders (helpfulness_ratio, score_vs_product_avg). Because the strongest 'confounders' are mixed with a mediated/collider-heavy set and one confounder is effectively the treatment's own definition, the confounder_quality is only moderate."
}
